doc.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013

title: Stanley Crouch, Giddins and Gitler visit Buffalo; Al Tinney
summary: Anecdotes about hosting critics, Crouch's grouchiness at Mark Murphy's show, and Gitler interviewing Al Tinney.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Really. A pain in the neck and a funny guy?

Oh yeah. He’s a grouch. He thinks he’s got all the answers and everything. So I remember I had Mark Murphy singing with Sonny Rollins. And he comes behind, in the room behind, while Mark is singing, doing a whole tribute to Miles and to Clifford Brown. And he goes, “So what’s this guy got on Joe Williams?” Like that. I go, “What’s he got on Joe Williams, they’re friends. Why? What’s the problem?” “He ain’t got nothin’ on Joe Williams.” I said, “well he scats a lot better than Joe Williams, but Joe has this beautiful baritone voice and everything else. And I don’t know that they’re in competition except with you.” And I invited these guys to my house and everything. And I had done a lecture/presentation of jazz singing. And he and Giddons and Gitler and one other guy, came to the talk. I did a three screen lecture. And we were talking about different styles of jazz singing. It was right on. And they walked out because they wanted to get some food. I said, well, what do I know, because I’m only from Buffalo, and you are the mother-fuckers from New York City. And believe me, I knew ten times what Giddons knew back then, and then same thing with Crouch. Because they were off-base on a lot of things. I had Al Tinney here. And Al Tinney was the one who ran those things at Clark Monroe’s. And he made his home here, and he was a gentle spirit too.
Yes. I did an interview with him.
Oh, so you know. He would never brag or anything else. And so Ira sees Sammy Noto and sees Sam Falzone, who just died last week —

Yeah. Sweet. He was in a Hospice. And he goes, “Chuck, is that Al Tinney?” I go, “Yeah.” He says, “I’m working on my second book on bebop. You think I can get an interview with him.” I was thinking if you weren’t a friend of Carleton’s I’d say go fuck yourself. But I didn’t say it. I treated those guys great. I had great sandwiches in my house. My mother — and he was a funny guy, I’ve got to admit. But yeah, so Gitler did this nice interview with Al, and did a 2-1/2 page part of his second bop book about that. So Gitler liked ice hockey. He was a big ice hockey guy. But anyway, they treated Mark real shabby. He’s a faggot with a bad wig.
